\[
\begin{gathered}
\begin{bmatrix} R' \\ G' \\ B' \end{bmatrix} =
\begin{bmatrix}
0.213 + 0.787 s & 0.715 - 0.715 s & 0.072 - 0.072 s \\
0.213 - 0.213 s & 0.715 + 0.285 s & 0.072 - 0.072 s \\
0.213 - 0.213 s & 0.715 - 0.715 s & 0.072 + 0.928 s
\end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} R \\ G \\ B \end{bmatrix},
\qquad s = \frac{ 150 }{100}
\end{gathered}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(R, G, B\): The encoded channel values from 0 to 255
- \(s\): The saturation factor
- \(Y\): The gray value with the weights of the spec

This is the matrix of the CSS saturate() function in the W3C Filter Effects spec. It equals C' = Y + s (C - Y) for each channel C, with the gray Y = 0.213 R + 0.715 G + 0.072 B. So s = 0 gives gray, s = 1 keeps the image, and s above 1 pushes each color away from its gray. The gray Y itself does not change. The matrix acts on the encoded sRGB values from 0 to 255, and the results are clipped to 0 to 255.
